articles.summary: Wwalmart is offering a solid deal on a prebuilt desktop computer that excels at 1080p and 1440p gaming. For a limited time you can pick up a brand new MSI Codex R2 RTX 5070 gaming PC for just $1,449 with free shipping. It's sold and shipped from Walmart direct and not a marketplace vendor.
body: The MSI Codex R2 gaming PC is equipped with an air-cooled Intel Core Ultra 7 265F CPU, GeForce RTX 5070 12GB GPU, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 1TB M.2 SSD. The Intel Core Ultra 7 265F is a 20-core processor with a max boost clock of 5.3GHz. This is a solid all-purpose CPU for both gaming and multi-tasking. A 750W PSU powers the system.

The GeForce RTX 5070 is the best Nvidia card for 1080p and 1440p gaming and by itself this card retails for $600 (although generally it's higher these days). It's also powerful enough to run most games at 4K, although at that point you'll see noticeable gains jumping up to a 5070 Ti. Compared to the previous generation GPUs, the RTX 5070 offers a slight performance improvement over the RTX 4070 Super, which was and still is an excellent GPU. The fps gain is greater in games that support DLSS 4.5 with multi-frame generation. Check out our RTX 5070 review.

articles.title: Fanttik Has a Great Deal on an All-in-One Electric Air Duster and Power Bank
articles.summary: Fanttik has a pretty cool accessory that covers both maintenance and energy recharge in one compact device. For a limited time, you can pick up the Fanttik B10 Pro Max Electric Air Duster and Power Bank for $44.99 with free shipping after you apply coupon code " IGNB10PM ".
body: The Fanttik B10 Pro Max is first and foremost an electric air duster. This palm-sized device features a 130,000 RPM brushless fan that pushes air at a velocity of 65m/s with a "megaboost" button for an extra surge of airflow. There are six levels of intensity, and the highest level is more than enough power to clear out the dust from your PC or the grime from your keyboard. Four different nozzles are included, including one that allows you to fill air up in inflatables.

Two 4,000mAh batteries (8,000mAh total) allows you to use the air duster cordlessly, and therein lies its second use an 8,000mAh power bank. You don't want to use this as your main battery backup for your electronics, since it's bulkier than your typical power bank and the USB-C port only has a maximum output of 10W. However, it's quite useful in a pinch, and I'm not sure why other electric air dusters don't have this functionality since nearly all of them run off lithium batteries. The USB-C connectivity means it is natively compatible with most devices, including your iPhone 18 or Nintendo Switch.
points: Fanttik has a pretty cool accessory that covers both maintenance and energy recharge in one compact device.

articles.summary: Between WandaVision and Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, Wanda Maximoff (Elizabeth Olsen) demonstrated just how far grief could drive someone with the power to rewrite reality to do terrible things.
body: Marvel's new Disney Plus series, VisionQuest, follows White Vision (Paul Bettany) as he grapples with his identity. Following Vision’s death in Avengers: Infinity War, S.W.O.R.D. rebuilt the synthezoid as an emotionless weapon, but Hex Vision (the version created by Wanda in Westview) was able to unlock his memories during their confrontation in WandaVision. The first two episodes of VisionQuest were released Tuesday night. In them, we learn that Vision has tried to live a peaceful, quiet life in Edinburgh. At night, he interacts with various other artificial intelligences — like J.A.R.V.I.S., F.R.I.D.A.Y., and even Ultron — existing in a mindscape he’s created for himself.

articles.title: Peak Has Been Leaked for PS5 by the ESRB
articles.summary: The beloved co-op adventure game, Peak, has been leaked for PS5 by the ESRB. Last year, an adorable, cheap co-op game known as Peak blew up on Steam. In the game, players unite with their friends to pass through a wide variety of deadly obstacles in order to climb absurdly tall mountains.
body: It seems like the game will likely only continue to grow its audience, as the ESRB has rated Peak for PS5. Historically, ESRB leaks are incredibly accurate, so it seems like only a matter of time before an official announcement is made. As of right now, it's unclear if Peak will also come to Xbox and Nintendo Switch 2, but it would be surprising if this remained console exclusive to PS5.

Unfortunately for new players, Peak ended its post-launch support earlier this summer. As a result, you probably shouldn't expect the game to receive any significant content after it releases on console. It's also unclear if it will enjoy the same exceptionally low price when it does hit consoles, but it would be surprising if the team behind the game changed it. Following the game's release, the team noted that there's a psychology behind pricing a game that low.

articles.title: 'VisionQuest' Just Officially Fixed a Huge Problem With MCU Canon
articles.summary: Finally, adamantium is being put to good use in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Well, not good use, but at least someone is using it now, which has taken way, way too long.
body: In the second episode of VisionQuest, which debuted Oct. 13 on Disney Plus alongside episode 1, the assassin Paladin (Todd Stashwick) uses adamantium bullets to do some real damage to Vision — or, White Vision (is that really what we're calling him?). This marks the first time someone has actually made use of adamantium in the main timeline of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, despite the fact that Disney bought Fox — and with it, the ability to use adamantium in storylines — way back in 2019.

Adamantium, of course, has commonly been an X-Men thing, as it is most famously the metal that Wolverine’s skeleton is coated with. Wolverine’s claws being made of adamantium goes back to his very first appearance, when he fought the Hulk in The Incredible Hulk issue 181 from 1974. In that comic, Wolverine’s claws were merely a part of his gloves, not originating from his actual body, but he does state that they’re made from “diamond-hard adamantium.”

articles.title: Hideo Kojima Reviews The Resident Evil Movie
articles.summary: Writer-director Hideo Kojima has seen Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, and he has now shared his review. Kojima, a true cinephile known for his public movie reviews, said he "wasn't particularly interested" in seeing the movie at first, but he did, and he sounded pretty impressed by what he saw.
body: "Right from the opening, it hits you with music reminiscent of The Thing. From there, it’s a relentless barrage of classic horror techniques, terrifying situations, and jump scares that never lets up until the very end," he said.

Kojima went on to observe what others did as well, which is how the Resident Evil movie is more of a film that provides the "experience of playing Resident Evil" as opposed to watching an adaptation of one of its stories.

"It reminded me of how I felt when I first played the original Resident Evil on PlayStation back in 1996," he said. "I was just like [main character] Bryan in this movie. I kept getting game over after game over, shouting “F***!” over and over again. lol."

This is the kind of response that Cregger said he wanted viewers to have. It's also what got Cregger in some hot water with hardcore fans who wanted to see a straight adaptation of one of the games instead of Cregger's own original story set inside the world of Resident Evil.
points: Writer-director Hideo Kojima has seen Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, and he has now shared his review.

articles.title: 5 Forgotten Square Enix RPGs That Deserve a Comeback
articles.summary: Square Enix is synonymous with fantastic role-playing games, thanks to series like Final Fantasy, Dragon Quest, and Kingdom Hearts. But very few games are lucky enough to enjoy that kind of longevity.
body: Here are a handful of Square Enix RPGs that deserve a comeback, whether it's simply a port for modern hardware, an attentive remaster, or a full-on remake. These games may not have been forgotten by fans, but all of them have suffered a bit of neglect from the developer-publisher, for one reason or another.

Parasite Eve inspired a couple sequels — 1999's Parasite Eve 2 and 2010's The Third Birthday for PlayStation Portable — but the original feels especially ripe for rediscovery today. The two games that inspired it are more popular than ever, and the action-oriented combat system was ahead of its time. Heck, Square Enix could repeat history and use the FF7 Remake engine for a reimagined Parasite Eve.

articles.title: Red Dead’s Shocking Twist Ending Angered A Lot Of People, But It Was The Right Call, Rockstar Co-Founder Says
articles.summary: Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser has recalled the controversial ending to 2010's Red Dead Redemption in which the main character, John Marston, is killed. He said in an interview that the game's lead designer, Christian Cantamessa was on board with the idea to kill off Marston, but Houser wondered…
body: "So I said, ‘I think maybe we have to kill him.’ And he goes, ‘That's a great idea. Got to do it.’ I said, ‘I don't know if… let me just think about this,’ because we're just dealing with audio and dialogue," Houser told IGN "The nature of an open-world game is you finish a story, then you go back into the world and wrap up all the side content if you want to. We'd have to play as someone else for that. We could play as Jack, but what does that mean? So I had to think through for a while what it would mean production-wise.”

How Rockstar handled it was by setting RDR's epilogue years later, in the year 1914, with players taking control of Marston's son, Jack. He said this setup presented challenges, too, in terms of the technical realities of playing as Jack as opposed to John. There were story and mission concerns, too, including how multi-stage missions might play out if players, as John, completed one part and then came back to finish later as Jack.
"How would that work? We had to think through all of that stuff and concluded we could probably make it work, but we were still scared," he said.

articles.title: 11 Magic: The Gathering Marvel Cards That Perfectly Capture Their Characters
articles.summary: That’s what makes Universes Beyond, Wizards of the Coast’s line of crossover sets, such a compelling experiment. Bringing beloved characters into Magic is one thing, but translating what makes them special into the game’s mechanics is an entirely different challenge.
body: One of the most interesting things about Magic: The Gathering is how a well-designed card can tell you everything you need to know about a character without requiring a single line of exposition. A clever ability, a specific gameplay restriction, or even a minor mechanical detail can capture what makes a character so memorable, distilling their defining traits into something you can actually experience at the table. When a card’s abilities tell a story that fans already know, the result can be more satisfying than any amount of flavor text.

With Marvel Super Heroes bringing the likes of the Avengers, the X-Men, and some of Marvel’s most formidable villains to the battlefield, there are plenty of contenders for the set’s most inspired designs. These are the cards that capture their subjects so perfectly through gameplay that it’s difficult to imagine a better way to represent them.

articles.title: Valve is clearing out its discontinued Index VR headsets if you want a cheap piece of history
articles.summary: With the recently launched Steam Frame superseding the Index VR headset, Valve has heavily discounted remaining stock of the latter. The Index VR headset launched in 2019 for $499, but now you can get one for $399.20.
body: Keep in mind that the Index VR headset doesn't come with controllers or a base station. A package bundling those used to cost $999, but that option is no longer available and thus, there's no associated discount.

Left controller replacements and replacement tethers are going for $119.20 and $103.20 respectively. No, there aren't any right controller replacements listed. It seems that if you want controllers for your Index VR, you'll probably need to buy them elsewhere. The same goes for base stations.

"Valve Index is no longer being produced," reads a Steam news item published earlier today. "Remaining Index headsets, controllers, and accessories are still available at the new prices below while supplies last."

That "while supplies last" is crucial: obviously Valve won't be making any more, and they've given no sense of how many they have lying around. If you really want one, perhaps as a collectible, I'd probably act fast.

articles.title: Kojima says he was 'just like Bryan' from the Resident Evil movie when he played RE1 in 1996: 'I kept getting game over after game over, shouting F***!'
articles.summary: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil film was released to critical acclaim last month, with more than one reviewer calling it ' the best videogame movie ever.' Another review dropped today, from none other than Hideo Kojima, and it's (seemingly) a glowing one.
body: "I wasn’t particularly interested at first, but since it’s Zach Cregger’s latest film, I went to see Resident Evil," Kojima posted on Twitter on October 12.

"Right from the opening, it hits you with music reminiscent of "The Thing." From there, it’s a relentless barrage of classic horror techniques, terrifying situations, and jump scares that never lets up until the very end."

That bit is sorta why I said seemingly above. Do I detect a little backhanded praise? Calling it a "relentless barrage" isn't necessarily a compliment, saying a director used "classic horror techniques" could be a way of saying it's unoriginal, and pointing out that there are "jump scares" throughout might suggest it's not a particularly sophisticated film.
Or, maybe I'm coloring Kojima's statements with my own paranoia which endlessly scans any compliment I'm given for potential criticism. You be the judge.

body: The update has drawn some concern from players waiting for the promised Switch 2 Witcher 3 update, prompting the studio to reassure people on X that: "We're working on getting the Nintendo Switch 2 patch to all users as soon as possible." That Switch 2 patch is said to improve visual "clarity and sharpness" in the game.

CD Projekt Red has been busy addressing issues with the Remastered edition of The Witcher 3 since it was released two weeks ago. It's a transformative update, significantly altering the game's visuals while also changing animations, skills, and even some gameplay. Given its breadth - and that it's free and occurring 11 years after the game's release - I called The Witcher 3 Remastered an extraordinarily generous upgrade after playing it, though the game's audience isn't entirely happy. Some feel it made the game too bright, though this aspect has been addressed in patches since release.

The Specialist Pack pre-order bonus, available for all pre-ordered editions, gives you the opportunity to unlock these early. There are three upgrades to choose from, but you can only equip one at a time – choose wisely!
points: Pre-orders for METRO 2039 are now open, and we are revealing the editions that will be available on launch day, come February 4th 2027!
